summary: A 1934 steel fire tower beside Highway 67 near Jacob Lake that visitors can climb to the catwalk. Builders and height are disputed across sources.

facts.design: Aermotor steel tower with a 7 x 7 ft metal cab; height given as 80 ft by markers and Wikipedia and 100 ft by the register

access.note: Visitors may climb 123 open steps to the catwalk below the cab. Entry into the cab itself is restricted. No Forest Service page checked for climbing rules.

visit.trail_note: Stands beside Grand Canyon Highway (Arizona Route 67) at Jacob Lake. Climb is by steps to the catwalk below the cab.

events.note: Steel tower erected. Builders disputed: Civilian Conservation Corps per Wikipedia and one marker; Kanab contractors per the register

corrections.why: The two markers and Wikipedia give 80 feet, about 24.4 m. The register gives 100 feet (30.5 m). The record's 24.7 m matches neither figure, so a human should check where it came from.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia and one marker credit the Civilian Conservation Corps; the register credits the Kanab contractors who built Big Springs. The sources do not reconcile this, so the story reports both.

sources.title: Jacob Lake Lookout Tower Historical Marker

notes_for_editor: The register's 2020 visit report (Michael King, October 9, 2020) says 'Staffed? No'. The GrandCanyon.com listing says the tower is generally staffed mid-May to mid-October, which overlaps the visit date, so the seasonal picture is unclear. Height: markers and Wikipedia say 80 ft, the register says 100 ft; brief's 24.7 m is in the corrections list for a human to decide. Builder: CCC versus Kanab contractors is unresolved; the NRHP nomination is a scanned PDF with no text layer on NPGallery, so it could not be read. The climbing claim rests on Wikipedia and a tourism listing; no Forest Service page was read, so the climb is not confirmed by the agency. Brief's elevation 2478 m matches the register.
